messages:
alex: Hey — running into intermittent hangs in the Go client when cancelling streaming requests. We cancel the request context but connections sometimes appear to stay active and goroutines pile up. After ~200 cancels we exhaust the pool. Anyone seen this?

maria: How are you creating the client/transport? any relevant timeouts or Dialer config?

alex: Minimal repro:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: true,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// we cancel from another goroutine after ~1s when user aborts
cancel()
// sometimes we see goroutines stuck reading from transport after cancel
```

ben: Do you close / drain resp.Body in the cancel path? If you just cancel and never call resp.Body.Close() the underlying stream may not be reusable.

alex: We call resp.Body.Close() but only after the request returns. The problem is the client.Do often never returns — it's stuck in the HTTP/2 read loop (stack shows `(*http2clientConn).readFrame` / `framer.ReadFrame`).

sam: This rings a bell — there was a subtle interaction where canceled HTTP/2 streams could hang if server kept the stream open and the client wasn't explicitly closed/drained. Two things to check: make sure you cancel the request context AND call resp.Body.Close() from the goroutine that's waiting on the request. Also add a hard read timeout so client.Do can't hang forever.

ravi: For production we've found some good knobs: set `IdleConnTimeout`, `TLSHandshakeTimeout`, and also configure a `net.Dialer` with a `Timeout` and `KeepAlive`. Example: 
```go
dialer := &net.Dialer{Timeout: 5*time.Second, KeepAlive: 30*time.Second}
tr := &http.Transport{
  DialContext: dialer.DialContext,
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: true,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 20,
  IdleConnTimeout: 15*time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 5*time.Second,
  ResponseHeaderTimeout: 3*time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```
These reduce the blast radius when something stalls.

maria: Another defensive pattern: spawn the request and read loop in a goroutine and use a select with a timer/context to forcibly close the body if cancelled. Example helper: 
```go
func drainAndClose(r io.ReadCloser){
  io.Copy(io.Discard, io.LimitReader(r, 1<<20))
  r.Close()
}

// usage after cancel: go drainAndClose(resp.Body)
```
That lets underlying streams be returned to the pool.

ben: Also check Go version and x/net/http2. We've seen fixes in newer releases where canceled streams left the connection in a weird state. Upgrading fixed a flakey repro for us.

alex: Good call — our infra is on go1.19.3. I'll try 1.20+ on a branch. Any suggestions for auth token refresh during long-lived streams? We sometimes refresh a token mid-stream which seems to trigger 401s and the server holds the stream.

sam: Ideally avoid mid-stream auth refresh. If you must, do it out-of-band and establish a new stream after refresh. If server returns 401 for a streaming request, make sure you close the body on client and create a new request (don't rely on retry on the same stream).

ravi: One more runtime knob: lower `MaxIdleConnsPerHost` if you want faster recycling of connections under heavy cancel churn. We run 10-20 for high churn streaming; higher counts hide the leak longer but increase resource usage. Also `ResponseHeaderTimeout` helps fail fast on stuck responses.

maria: Can you paste a small goroutine stack snippet when it hangs? that helps triage whether it's in `readFrame` or blocked on `conn.Read`.

alex: pasted below — looks like: 
```
 goroutine 12345 [IO wait]:
 net.(*netFD).read(...)
 net.(*conn).Read(...)
 crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read(...)
 net/http.(*http2ClientConnReadLoop).readFrame(...)
 golang.org/x/net/http2.(*clientConn).readFrame(...)
```

ben: That matches old reports. Steps to mitigate: 1) upgrade Go/x/net/http2, 2) add ResponseHeaderTimeout + IdleConnTimeout, 3) ensure you close/drain bodies on cancel, and 4) consider a small integration test that cancels many concurrent streaming requests to reproduce.

ci-bot: Added GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4829 (repro + goroutine stacks) :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks — I'll try the upgrades + timeouts and push a repro test. Will ping for review when I have a branch.

sam: Happy to review the test. If you can't upgrade Go right away, adding the timeouts + explicit drain is a good short-term mitigation. :thumbsup:

alex: Great, creating a draft PR now.
